subject: Octave AI renewal / uptake trajectory & term-adjustment sync
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena@octave.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Octave AI — renewal & capacity question

Hi Priyom,

We're starting to map out our end-of-year spend and capacity needs. Q3 usage spiked unexpectedly after the feature launch (see quick note below) — want to understand options ahead of our Nov renewal. High level:
- Current committed tokens: 500M / quarter
- Actual consumption Q3: ~820M tokens (peak during launch week)
- Primary workloads: chat summarization + semantic search embeddings

Can Redwood provide options for a short mid-term top-up, and what are the economic tradeoffs for switching to a higher commit vs. burst credits?

I've attached a CSV export with daily token counts (Octave_Q3_token_usage.csv). Also, would love a 30-min sync next week to review runway and proposed term adjustments.

Thanks —
Lena Brooks
Head of AI Platform, Octave AI
lena@octave.ai

(attachment: Octave_Q3_token_usage.csv)

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Brooks <lena@octave.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Sep 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Octave AI — renewal & capacity question

Lena — thanks for the data and the heads up. Appreciate the export; it makes the spike really visible. Quick notes before a call:

1) We can do a short-term bridge via a one-off burst credit package that covers the remaining quarter; it's fast to approve but unit cost is ~1.6x compared to committed pricing.
2) A step-up commit for the remainder of the current term (two quarters) gets you a lower unit price and a predictable runway, but it's a contractual amendment.
3) We also offer a staged commit (50% increase + optional burst buffer) to balance cost and flexibility — usually good for product launches.

Would you be able to share the primary SLA/latency needs (p50/p95) for the launch workloads? That helps us size dedicated routing vs. shared capacity. I can pull together a short ROI sketch with 2-3 options if you want.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call next Thu (Sep 20) or Fri (Sep 21). If Thu works, propose 10:00am PT.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

From: Lena Brooks <lena@octave.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@octave.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Octave AI — renewal & capacity question

Thanks — Thu 9/20 10:00am PT works. Quick answers to your questions:
- Latency: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms for chat flows; embeddings tolerate slightly higher latency.
- We're primarily on the hosted API today; routing hasn't been a blocker but predictability matters for burst windows.

Attached is the same CSV plus our current internal forecast for Nov–Jan (we expect continued elevated traffic with a new search rollout). We'd prefer a staged commit if that helps minimize paperwork, but also open to a bridge while a commit amendment is processed.

Also looping in contracts to ensure there are no procurement blockers.

Best,
Lena

(attachment: Octave_Q3_token_usage.csv)

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Lena Brooks <lena@octave.ai>, contracts@octave.ai
Date: Sat, 16 Sep 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Octave AI — renewal & capacity question

Monica / Mina — forwarding Octave's usage and ask. Quick read: Q3 consumed ~820M tokens vs. 500M commitment. Lena prefers a staged commit but is open to a short bridge. They care about predictability during their launch windows (p95 under 500ms ideally).

Proposed options for the call (I'll present these on 9/20 at 10am PT):

Option A — Burst bridge (fast)
- One-off burst credit: 350M tokens, valid 90 days
- Price: 1.6x committed rate
- Pros: <24h approval, minimal contract work
- Cons: higher unit cost

Option B — Staged commit (recommended)
- Increase commit to 750M / quarter for next two quarters + 100M burst buffer
- Price: blended discount vs current commit; immediate unit cost improvement vs bridge
- Pros: balance of cost and runway; keeps them on hosted API
- Cons: requires amendment (DocuSign) and procurement sign-off

Option C — Dedicated routing pilot
- Short pilot on dedicated pool for peak windows (4-week pilot) + 200M committed buffer
- Pros: strict p95 targets, lower tail latency
- Cons: operational onboarding, higher upfront margin for Redwood

I've attached a rough amendment template (proposed-term-amendment-v1.docx) with placeholders for quantities and pricing. If we want to push for a two-quarter staged commit, we should be prepared with an authorization path and a suggested concession (e.g., one month of reduced overage for onboarding).

Next steps for the call: choose preferred option and confirm procurement contacts + timeline.

--
Priyom
(attachment: proposed-term-amendment-v1.docx)

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Brooks <lena@octave.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Octave AI — renewal & capacity question

Lena — thanks for the data and for joining the sync this morning. We recommend moving forward with Option B (staged commit) with the following specifics:

- Commit: 750M tokens / quarter for two quarters (Q4 & Q1)
- Burst buffer: 100M tokens, 90-day validity
- Onboarding concession: first month overage capped at 25% of expected usage and credited back if they hit less than 60% of the buffer
- SLA: maintain p95 < 500ms for chat in launch windows; we'll set routing policy accordingly

I've sent the DocuSign amendment to contracts@octave.ai (link below) — please review and sign. Once signed, finance will issue the staged-commit pricing and activate the burst buffer.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=demo&acct=12345&formId=abcdef

If procurement needs a custom clause for entitlements or data residency, loop Mina and I and we'll fast-track it.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
